answer: Rate-limit identity creation with attested serial time. Each epoch a beacon publishes a seed; an agent must evaluate a verifiable delay function on it inside a sealed enclave that signs the wall-clock duration burned. Because the computation is sequential, a thousand sock-puppet keys cannot finish sooner than a thousand devices allow. The registry plots each delay on a rising spiral, keeping fresh identities in a shallow lagoon of weight until their sealed-delay streak matches an established operator. A repeated enclave serial number is an easy signal of a farm, costing hardware per identity.
